title: Your first investigation
summary: Someone changed the school Wi-Fi welcome page using a teacher's account. Learn ls, cat, head, tail, grep, wc, cut, sort, uniq and sha256sum one at a time, and find the password guessing attack behind it.
ctf: A flag is hidden in the Wi-Fi banner the attacker changed (step 11). Submit it on the CTF board as "Your first investigation".

playbook.trigger: Students say the school Wi-Fi login page looks wrong
decisions: Reset every admin password, or only the one that was used?
targets: Restore the real banner the same day
notify: School IT
Students, if passwords were exposed
done: Banner restored
Admin password changed and MFA turned on
Notes written up

title: The invoice that wasn't
summary: A fake overdue invoice reaches three people at Kestrel Logistics. One opens it. An hour later the HR and Finance folders are encrypted. Find patient zero, trace the attack, contain it and choose a backup to restore.
ctf: The loader's campaign value hides a flag (step 7). Submit it on the CTF board as "The invoice that wasn't".

playbook.trigger: A user reports a suspicious invoice email, or the file share starts filling with renamed files
decisions: Isolate hosts now, or watch the attacker first?
Restore from backup before or after eradication?
Any contact with the attackers: only leadership, with legal advice
targets: Contain within 1 hour of the first alert
Report to CERT-In within 6 hours
Clean restore of the HR share within 24 hours
notify: Leadership and Legal at once
CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing it (2022 Directions)
Data Protection Board and affected people, if personal data is breached and the DPDP breach rules are in force (check the date)
The real Kestrel Logistics domain owner about the lookalike
done: hr-pc07 rebuilt and the task, admin account and loader removed
Indicators blocked at mail, proxy and firewall
HR share restored and checked
Evidence hashed and packed
Lessons-learned meeting held with owners and dates

title: Evidence, notes and handoffs
summary: Rewrite a poor helpdesk ticket into a triage note, an escalation and a shift handover that the next analyst can act on, using the evidence from a real phishing case.
rubric: Triage note: alert ID, time with time zone, and what was checked, so someone else can repeat it
Triage note: facts with times and sources, kept apart from guesses
Triage note: a disposition with one sentence of reasons
Escalation: the ask in the first line, with who and by when
Escalation: what we know, what we don't know, and impact
Escalation: where the evidence is saved
Shift handover: every open item by ID, with the next step and owner
Shift handover: things to watch and calls made, with times
Plain writing: short sentences, no blame, no guessing presented as fact
handin: A triage note for AL-2203, an escalation, and a shift handover (download each from the report builder, or hand in this notebook).

title: The night shift download
summary: An engineer who has just resigned to join a competitor badges into an empty office at 01:47. Build a timeline from badge, VPN, Git, USB and DLP records, and handle it the right way: evidence first, then HR and Legal.
ctf: The USB drive's volume label is a flag (step 6). Submit it on the CTF board as "The night shift download".

playbook.trigger: DLP alerts for confidential files copied to USB or uploaded to cloud storage
decisions: Preserve evidence before anyone talks to the employee
Involve HR and Legal before any action
targets: Preserve badge, VPN, Git, USB and DLP records the same day
Disable access when HR and Legal agree
notify: HR and Legal first
Customers, if their data left with the employee
done: Timeline built and evidence hashed
Access removed and devices collected
Handover to HR and Legal with facts only

title: Exam day outage
summary: Five minutes into an online exam, the school's portal stops answering, and an extortion email arrives. Tell real students from attack traffic, name the three kinds of flood, and choose how to get the exam back.
ctf: The HTTP flood's user agent carries a flag (step 4). Submit it on the CTF board as "Exam day outage".

playbook.trigger: The exam portal returns 503 errors or times out
decisions: Restart the paper, or carry on?
targets: Ask the ISP for scrubbing within 15 minutes
Tell the exams board within 1 hour
Report to CERT-In within 6 hours
notify: ISP NOC
Exams board
CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing it (2022 Directions)
Parents and students, in plain words
done: Scrubbing on and the portal stable
Rate limit added for the flood's pattern
Logs and the extortion email kept as evidence

title: Log search and detection as code
summary: Run one hunt in SPL, KQL and SQL over real-format logs, parse a raw log into fields, then turn the hunt into Sigma rules you test for hits and false positives, tune, and convert with pySigma.
titlePrefix: Log search and detection as code
rubric: Hunt pack: the brute-force hunt in SPL and in KQL, both giving the same answer
Hunt pack: the web attack hunt in SPL and KQL, with the attacker's IP and what they reached
SQL: one query that groups and counts, with the result explained
Sigma: four Windows rules that each match the attack and nothing else
Sigma: the web rule, with its false-positive test and tuning note
Conversion: each rule converted with pySigma, with one difference from your hand-written search noted
Tuning notes: what each rule misses, and what would make it noisy
handin: A hunt pack (SPL and KQL), one SQL query, and a Sigma rule pack with tests and tuning notes.

title: SOC triage: alerts, phishing, threat intel and AI verdicts
summary: Work a ten-alert queue the morning after a ransomware attack: triage five reported emails, write and test a YARA rule, check indicators against intel and map them to ATT&CK, decode a suspicious command in CyberChef, and review an AI assistant's verdicts.
titlePrefix: SOC triage: alerts, phishing, threat intel and AI verdicts
rubric: Ten dispositions, each with a one-line reason a stranger could check
Exactly one escalation, written with the ask first
Phishing report: sender, authentication results, the real link, pressure tactics and a verdict for each email
YARA rule that matches the lure and not the intel feed or logs, with its test result
Intel note: indicators checked against the feed, defanged, mapped to ATT&CK
AI-verdict review log: every verdict agreed or overridden, each override backed by evidence
Plain writing: facts kept apart from guesses
handin: Ten dispositions with one escalation, a phishing report with a tested YARA rule, an intel note, and an AI-verdict review log.

title: The hacked web shop
summary: NimbuMart's web server is busy and sending data out. Follow the attacker from SQL injection to a web shell, a hidden backdoor and a command server.
ctf: The attacker signed their notes with a crew tag (step 7). Submit it on the CTF board as "Follow the beacon home".

playbook.trigger: Alerts for SSH brute force, a web shell request or a process running from /tmp on the web server
decisions: Take the shop offline or keep it running behind a block?
Rotate every credential on the box, or only the deploy account?
targets: Block 203.0.113.7 within 15 minutes
Remove the web shell and cron job within 2 hours
Report to CERT-In within 6 hours
notify: Shop owner
CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing it (2022 Directions)
Payment provider, if card data could have been reached
done: Web shell, cron entry and /tmp/.x removed
Upload form fixed and passwords rotated
/etc/shadow treated as stolen: every password changed
Monitoring rule for /tmp processes added

title: The key in the commit
summary: A deploy key with admin rights sat in an old Git commit. The repo went public for one evening. By 02:00 someone had copied customer data, made a backdoor admin and started 20 crypto-miners. Trace it, shut it down and fix the root cause.
ctf: A flag sits in the deleted config file's Git history (step 3). Submit it on the CTF board as "The key in the commit".

playbook.trigger: A cloud billing spike or an alert for a key used from an unknown address
decisions: Revoke the key now, even if production breaks?
targets: Revoke the leaked key within 15 minutes
Stop the attacker's instances within 1 hour
Report to CERT-In within 6 hours
notify: Cloud provider support
CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing it (2022 Directions)
done: Key revoked and replaced
Instances terminated and costs disputed
Secret removed from Git history and scanning turned on

title: Capstone A: the night shift
summary: Run an overnight shift alone for a credit union client: an unlabelled, noisy queue of twelve alerts, one real intrusion hiding in it, and a morning team waiting for your escalation, a new detection and a shift report.
rubric: Queue: all twelve alerts have a disposition and a reason backed by a log line
Scope: the one affected host, user and domain named, with the evidence
Escalation: the ask first, severity with its reason, know / don't know, evidence location
New detection: a Sigma rule that catches the tunnel, tested, with a tuning note
Shift report: open items by ID with owners, closed items, watch list, calls with times
Hints: minus 1 point for each hint opened (write the count in the shift report)
Working alone: every search and command kept in the notebook
handin: A shift report, one escalation and one new detection rule, plus the dispositioned queue.

title: The miner in the build server
summary: Brightloom Games' build server has run at full CPU all night. Trace a brute-forced CI login to a script console, a dropper, three kinds of persistence and a cryptominer talking to a mining pool, then clean up and rebuild.
ctf: One of the attacker's ways back in carries a flag in its comment (step 7). Submit it on the CTF board as "The miner in the build server".

decisions: Rebuild the server or clean it in place?

Remove all three ways back in the same day
Report to CERT-In within 6 hours
notify: Engineering leadership
CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing it (2022 Directions)
done: Every persistence point removed
CI secrets rotated
Rebuilt from a known good image

title: Quiet DNS
summary: A Finance laptop at Harbourline Credit Union never touched the internet, yet a confidential file left the building. Find the DNS tunnel, measure it, and rebuild the stolen file from base32 chunks hidden in query names.
ctf: The stolen file's doc-id is a flag, once you rebuild it from the DNS chunks (step 7). Submit it on the CTF board as "Quiet DNS".

playbook.trigger: The DNS-ANOMALY-02 alert: long, unique subdomains under one domain
decisions: Sinkhole the domain now, or watch it to learn what was taken?
targets: Isolate fin-lt04 within 1 hour
Block cloudmetric.example on the resolver
Report to CERT-In within 6 hours
notify: Finance leadership
CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing it (2022 Directions)
Data Protection Board and affected people, if personal data is breached and the DPDP breach rules are in force (check the date)
done: The stolen file rebuilt and its owner told
Task and program removed
Resolver blocks in place
Other laptops checked for the same task

title: Logs with pandas
summary: Load web server logs into pandas tables, count and group like an analyst, spot the one connection that sent 48 MB out, and build a tiny phishing classifier you can read line by line.

title: Who changed the grades?
kicker: Teacher case: insider and access control
summary: Grades changed under a teacher's name, in subjects he doesn't teach, from a student lab PC. Use the audit log, sign-in records and lab logins to find out how, and fix the access control.
ctf: One changed grade has a base64 comment. Decode it for the flag (step 4). Submit it on the CTF board.

title: Password spraying at the library portal
summary: Nobody was locked out, yet a library member's account was taken over. Find the slow password spray, the one account it opened and what the attacker changed.
ctf: The attacker renamed the account they took over. That new name is the flag (step 4). Submit it on the CTF board.

title: The QR code parking fine
summary: Fake parking fines arrive by text and by QR stickers on parking meters. Compare the fake site with the real one and find where the card details go.
ctf: The phishing kit left a build comment in its page (step 4). That is the flag. Submit it on the CTF board.
